hints: Since $PQ$ is horizontal and $P(1, 5)$ lies on circle centered at $(4, 1)$, $Q$ has $y = 5$. By symmetry across $x = 4$, $Q = (4 + 3, 5) = (7, 5)$.
walkthrough:
Equal heights on the circle give reflected points about its vertical centre line.
By horizontal symmetry across the vertical line through centre $(4, 1)$:
$$x_Q = 4 + (4 - 1) = 7, \quad y_Q = 5 \implies Q(7, 5)$$

Calculate tangent equations at $P(1, 5)$ and $Q(7, 5)$:
$$m_{CP} = -\dfrac{4}{3} \implies m_{\text{tan}, P} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies y - 5 = \dfrac{3}{4}(x - 1) \implies 3x - 4y = -17$$
$$m_{CQ} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies m_{\text{tan}, Q} = -\dfrac{3}{4} \implies y - 5 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 7) \implies 3x + 4y = 41$$

hints: Add the two tangent equations: $(3x - 4y) + (3x + 4y) = -17 + 41 \implies 6x = 24 \implies x = 4$.
walkthrough:
Equal heights on the circle give reflected points about its vertical centre line.
Solve the two tangent equations simultaneously:
$$3x - 4y = -17$$
$$3x + 4y = 41$$
Adding the equations: $$6x = 24 \implies x = 4$$

Substitute $x = 4$ into the second equation to find $y$:
$$3(4) + 4y = 41 \implies 12 + 4y = 41 \implies 4y = 29 \implies y = \dfrac{29}{4} = 7.25$$
$$T = \left(4, \dfrac{29}{4}\right)$$
